title: The 2:17 AM Incident
briefing_md:
Finvera is a digital wallet app with 3 million customers. Last night (15 October) this happened:

• 2:17 AM — the customer list was read in bulk by one of the company's own automatic programs.
• 2:23 AM — customers started getting an SMS: "Your wallet has been SUSPENDED". About 25,000 people got it before it stopped.
• 2:31 AM — the server that sends messages crashed.

No wallet was actually suspended, but the support phones are flooded. The head of security wants one answer by morning: were we hacked?

Your job: work out what really happened, what or who caused it, and how to stop it happening again.
root_cause_options: Human error during an approved change
Bad or wrongly formatted input data
Test or staging activity hitting production
twist_md: Two more documents have been found: the approved change request for last night, and a message from the on-call engineers' chat sent a few minutes after midnight.

lines: 23:41  Karthik (the on-call engineer) signed in from a laptop never seen before (LT-7F2). Location: Pune.
23:42  A confirmation request was sent to Karthik's phone — he APPROVED it.
23:42  Karthik is now connected to the company network.
23:58  Karthik opened the message server (prod-app-02).

messages.text: Phones are exploding. Customers say they got an SMS that their wallet is suspended.
Are we hacked?? Somebody saw a login from Pune on Karthik's account last night.
Twitter is saying Finvera got breached. Should we post something?
Status page is down too. This is 100% an attack.

rows: Replacement laptop — phone confirmation set up again at the IT desk

lines: 00:03  Karthik gave the reminder program (svc_notify) permission to read ALL customer details, for 24 hours. Reason written: "CHG-4471".
00:03  System check: Karthik is on call this week, so he is allowed to do this.
00:05  Karthik opened the list of automatic jobs on the message server.
00:05  New job added: run the "reengage" reminder program every night at 02:17.

evidence.title: Login attempts at the main server door

lines: 01:10  Someone at internet address 45.155.205.7 tried to log in as "root" — wrong password.
01:10  212 more wrong-password tries from the same address.
01:10  That address was automatically BLOCKED after 214 failed tries.

rows: Looked up customers who have not used the app for 90+ days

content.body_md:
Program: "reengage" — the "we miss you" reminder
What it does: finds customers who haven't used the app for 90+ days and sends them an SMS.

Which message it sends is decided by a setting called NOTIFY_TEMPLATE.
• The operations team must fill in NOTIFY_TEMPLATE on each server before the program is used.
• If NOTIFY_TEMPLATE is missing, the program uses its old built-in message: ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED (left over from the old "close inactive accounts" process).

If the SMS company refuses a batch, the program tries again immediately — forever — and writes every attempt into its record file.

content.subject: Batch accepted: 1 of 49
content.body_md:
Your batch was accepted and is being delivered.

Batch: 1 of 49 (1,000 people)
Message used: ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED
Preview: "Dear {name}, your Finvera wallet has been SUSPENDED due to inactivity. Call 1800-XXX to reactivate."

content.subject: REFUSED: batch 26 of 49
content.body_md:
Batch 26 of 49 was refused.

Reason: your hourly limit of 25,000 messages for sender FINVRA has been reached. Try again in 60 seconds.

lines: 02:26  Reminder program: SMS refused — trying again immediately. (This repeats thousands of times.)
02:28  The reminder program's record file is now 11.8 GB (normally a few MB). Automatic clean-up is only at 04:00.
02:31  ERROR: the server's disk is FULL — nothing more can be saved.
02:31  ERROR: the message service crashed and stopped.
02:29  WARNING: traffic spike — 12,440 requests per minute from a group of foreign addresses.
02:29  They were trying well-known break-in pages (/wp-login.php, /.env, /phpmyadmin).
02:29  The firewall answered every one with "page not found".

content.prompt: Summarise tonight's security events for the security head and give a verdict.
content.output:
Verdict: ACCOUNT TAKEOVER (high confidence).

1. Karthik's account logged in from a new laptop and a new city (Pune) at 23:42.
2. The account gave extra permissions to a program at 00:03.
3. A hidden night-time job was planted at 00:05 — a classic way attackers keep access.
4. Customer details were read in bulk at 02:17 and used for a fake SMS campaign.
5. Someone tried to break into the main server door at 01:10 — an active attacker.

Recommend: lock Karthik's account, change all passwords, report to the national cyber agency.

01:00  Website restarted in 1 second. No errors.

content.subject: APPROVED: CHG-4471 "We miss you" SMS — go live
content.body_md:
Change: run the "reengage" program every night at 02:17 on the message server, sending a "we miss you — here's a cashback offer" SMS to customers inactive for 90+ days.

Done by: Karthik (on call this week, working from home on replacement laptop LT-7F2)

Steps that must be done:
1. Give the reminder program permission to read customer details (24 hours only)
2. Set NOTIFY_TEMPLATE = REENGAGE_OFFER in the server settings file — BEFORE the first run

Approved by: Divya (Platform Lead)

messages.text: CHG-4471: permission given, nightly job added for 02:17. I'll add the NOTIFY_TEMPLATE line to the settings file in the morning — the first run is tomorrow night anyway.

answer.root_cause_md: Before the twist the evidence is designed to look like a break-in: a login from a new laptop and city (E01), a permission grant (E04), a new night-time job (E05), a bulk read of customers (E07), and an AI summary that says 'account takeover' (E13). Careful teams notice LT-7F2 is an IT-issued replacement laptop (E03), the phone confirmation was approved (E01), the permission cites change CHG-4471 (E04), the program falls back to ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED (E08) and the settings file has no NOTIFY_TEMPLATE (E14).
answer.post_twist_category: Human error during an approved change
answer.post_twist_responsible: Karthik carried out the approved change CHG-4471 but scheduled the reminder job for 02:17 the same night before setting NOTIFY_TEMPLATE, so it fell back to its ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED message and texted 48,210 inactive customers; after 25,000 SMS the hourly limit was hit, the endless retries filled the disk and crashed the message server. The login and permission change were legitimate.
